To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
α‐synuclein (α‐SYN) is resistant to degradation by proteinase K (a protease) only in specific brain regions of patients with Parkinson's disease, Lewy body dementia and related diseases.

αSYN in the brainstem-predinominant LB disease subtype was PK resistant in the substantia nigra and medulla, but not in the cerebral cortex, whereas αSYN in limbic subtype LB diseases was PK resistant in cingulate and para-hippocampal cortex and in frontal cortex in neocoertical subtype LB diseases.
Lewy body disease stage can be correlated with the regional distribution of PK-resistant αSYn.
